en: Taal Volcano is a rare volcano located on an island inside a lake that fills a much larger volcano crater.
Palawan is the oldest landmass in the Philippines, having formed from the Asian mainland millions of years before the other islands.
Mount Mayon in Albay is famous for having the most perfectly symmetrical volcanic cone in the entire world.
The Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped hills that turn brown during the dry season.
The Philippines sits in the Coral Triangle, which contains the highest diversity of marine fish and coral species on Earth.
The Philippines is the second-largest producer of geothermal energy in the world, harnessing heat from its many active volcanoes.
The Philippine Tarsier, found in Bohol, has eyes that are actually larger than its brain, giving it exceptional night vision.
The Philippines sits on the Pacific Typhoon Belt, causing it to experience an average of twenty tropical cyclones yearly.
The Philippines is an archipelago of exactly 7,641 islands, but only about 2,000 of them are permanently inhabited by people.
The massive 1991 eruption of Mount Pinatubo released so much ash that it temporarily cooled the average global temperature.
The Cagayan River is the longest river in the Philippines, stretching over 500 kilometers through the northeastern part of Luzon.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River is a unique cave river because it flows directly into the sea and experiences ocean tides.
